If you see content that is unlawful or breaches these terms (for example, a name, an alias or a photo), you can report it by writing to agustin.estevez.dominguez@gmail.com. We will review it and, where appropriate, remove it.

section5.title: 5. Golf competitions
section5.content:
The Service provides tools to organise amateur golf competitions, which are informal and for recreational purposes.

Handicaps, course data and maps partly come from third parties (such as the RFEG or OpenStreetMap) and may contain errors. Organisers are responsible for the rules of their competition and for ensuring fair play.

section7.content:
The Service is provided as is. We strive to keep it working well and continuously, but we cannot guarantee it will be free of interruptions or errors.

We are not liable for indirect damage arising from the use of the Service, except in cases of wilful misconduct or gross negligence. Nothing in these terms limits the rights the law grants to consumers and users.

section8.title: 8. Closing and suspending accounts
section8.content:
You can stop using the Service whenever you want and ask to close your account by writing to agustin.estevez.dominguez@gmail.com from your account's address; we will reply to your request within one month. When you close it, we deactivate your account and erase the personal data that is not linked to other players' results or competitions; your results, your scorecards and the competitions you have created are kept for as long as those competitions need them, as explained in the Privacy Policy.

We may suspend or close an account that breaches these terms seriously or repeatedly. Except in urgent cases (for example, a risk to other users' security), we will give you notice beforehand and explain why.

section9.title: 9. Changes to these terms
section9.content: If we change these terms, we will give you reasonable notice (by email or in the application) before they take effect. If you do not agree with the changes, you can close your account before that date.

section1.content:

section2.title: 2. Data we process
section2.content:
- Account: email, first and last name, alias, country and password, stored securely (hashed). If you sign in with Google, we receive your name, email and account identifier from Google.
- Gender: required to enrol in competitions, because each player's tees and categories depend on it.
- Golf: handicap (looked up with the RFEG at your request or entered manually) and chosen tees.
- Profile photo, if you choose to upload one.
- Friends: who you send or accept friend requests to or from.
- Activity and results: competitions and matches you take part in, scores, scorecards and statistics.
- Security: the devices you sign in from (browser and IP address) and sign-in attempts.
- Location: only when you allow it in your browser (see section 5).

section3.title: 3. Purposes and legal bases
section3.content:
- Providing the Service (creating and managing your account, organising competitions and matches, calculating results, showing leaderboards and sending the emails it needs, such as account verification or password reset): performance of the contract you accept when you sign up (art. 6.1.b GDPR).
- Protecting the Service and your account (device and sign-in attempt records, usage limits, abuse prevention) and detecting and fixing errors: legitimate interest in the security and proper operation of the Service (art. 6.1.f GDPR).
- Using your location to find nearby courses and measure distances on the course: your consent, given when you allow it in your browser and which you can withdraw at any time in its settings (art. 6.1.a GDPR).
- Complying with legal obligations, where they apply (art. 6.1.c GDPR).

We do not sell your data or use it for advertising.

section4.title: 4. Handicap and the RFEG
section4.content:
If your country is Spain, the Service looks up your handicap with the Royal Spanish Golf Federation (RFEG), using your first and last name to find you, in these cases:

- At your request, from your profile.
- When the organiser of a competition you are enrolled in launches or schedules a handicap update.
- Automatically when enrolment closes for a competition and, in Ryder-format competitions, when the captains are named.

It is not looked up for an enrolment where the organiser has set a custom handicap.

section5.title: 5. Location
section5.content: The Service only accesses your location when you allow it in your browser, and for two things: finding courses near you and measuring distances on the course during a round. Distances are calculated on your own phone. Your location is not used to track you and no history of your positions is kept.

section6.title: 6. What other users see
section6.content:
- Your friends see your name or alias, your photo and, if you turn it on, your achievements in their feed.
- Participants in a competition or match see your name, handicap, tees and results.
- In public competitions, the leaderboard and results can also be seen by people without an account, through the leaderboard link.

section7.title: 7. Providers and international transfers
section7.content:
We use these providers, which process data on our behalf, to run the Service:

- Render: hosting of the application and database (servers in the EU or the US depending on the service).
- Sentry: error tracking and Session Replay (Germany region, EU).
- Mailgun: email delivery (EU region).
- Cloudflare: content delivery network and attack protection (US).
- Google: sign-in with Google, if you use it (US).

When a provider processes data outside the European Economic Area, the transfer relies on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework or, failing that, on the standard contractual clauses approved by the European Commission.

In addition, when you view a hole map, your browser downloads the orthophotos directly from the public servers that publish them (IGN/PNOA, ICGC, geoEuskadi and IDENA), which receive your device's IP address, as with any website you visit.

section8.title: 8. Cookies, local storage and Session Replay
section8.content: We only use technical cookies (session, CSRF protection and device identification) and your browser's local storage for your preferences, such as the language. When an error occurs, Sentry may keep a recording of the session (Session Replay) with text masked and without images, so that we can fix it; the legal basis is our legitimate interest in the security and proper operation of the Service. The Cookie Policy has the details.

section9.title: 9. How long we keep data
section9.content:
We keep your data while your account is active.

If you ask to close your account, we deactivate it (it can no longer be used or signed in to) and erase the personal data that is not linked to other players' results or competitions. Data that is linked to them (your results and scorecards, and the competitions and matches you have created) is kept for as long as those competitions need it, because deleting it would alter other players' leaderboards and matches. If your account has none of that, it is deleted entirely.

We also keep any data the law requires us to keep, for the period it sets.

section10.title: 10. Your rights
section10.content:
You can exercise your rights of access, rectification, erasure, objection, restriction of processing and portability. You can view and correct much of your data yourself from your profile. Closing your account and portability (receiving your data in a structured format) are requested by email to agustin.estevez.dominguez@gmail.com, from your account's address. We reply to your request within one month; section 9 explains what is erased and what is kept when you close your account.

If you believe we have not handled your request properly, you have the right to lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD), at www.aepd.es.

section11.title: 11. Children
section11.content: The Service is not intended for children under 16 and signing up below that age is not allowed. If you believe a child under 16 has given us data, write to agustin.estevez.dominguez@gmail.com and we will delete it.

section12.title: 12. Changes to this policy
section12.content: If we change this policy in a significant way, we will give you notice in advance by email or in the application, and we will update the "Last updated" date.

section1.title: 1. What cookies are
section1.content: Cookies are small text files that a website stores on your device. We also use similar technologies, such as your browser's local storage (localStorage), to remember preferences.

section2.title: 2. Technical cookies we use
section2.content:
We only use technical cookies, needed for the Service to work, which do not require consent:

- Authentication cookies (httpOnly): access and refresh tokens that keep you signed in. They cannot be read from JavaScript.
- CSRF token cookie: protects against cross-site request forgery attacks.
- Device cookie (httpOnly, one year): identifies the device you sign in from, for device management and the security of your account.

In your browser's local storage we keep your preferences (language and interface) and data to keep scoring offline.

section3.title: 3. Cloudflare
section3.content: Cloudflare, which protects the Service against attacks and automated traffic, may set the technical security cookie __cf_bm, which tells people apart from bots and expires after 30 minutes. It is not used to track you or for advertising.

section4.title: 4. Sentry and Session Replay
section4.content: We use Sentry to detect and fix errors. When an error occurs, Sentry may keep a recording of the session (Session Replay): a recording of what happened on screen, with all text masked and without images, which helps us understand the failure. The data is hosted in the Germany region (EU). The legal basis is our legitimate interest in the security and proper operation of the Service. Sentry does not set advertising or tracking cookies.

section5.title: 5. Managing cookies
section5.content:
You can block or delete cookies in your browser settings. Bear in mind that without the technical cookies you will not be able to sign in or use the features that require it.

To delete the authentication cookies, use "Log out" in the application, which also invalidates your session.

section6.title: 6. Contact
section6.content: If you have questions about our use of cookies, write to agustin.estevez.dominguez@gmail.com or use the Contact page.
